evals.prompt: Build an internal linking plan for our landscaping company site https://verdantyards.ie. We have 6 service pages (garden design, lawn care, tree surgery, patios, irrigation, maintenance contracts), about 30 blog posts published over 2 years, a homepage, and a contact page. The blog posts almost never link to the service pages, they mostly link to each other or to nothing. Several older posts are not linked from anywhere since we redesigned the blog index last year. The service pages are what make us money.
evals.expected_output: An internal linking plan following the skill's output template: (1) the 6 service pages plus homepage and contact mapped and ranked as money pages with current and target inbound link counts; (2) an orphan detection step comparing the sitemap against a link-following crawl from the homepage, flagging the old posts stranded by the redesign and prescribing at least one inbound internal link from topically related content for each (zero orphans rule, since unlinked pages are rarely crawled and invisible to AI engines that retrieve through search indexes); (3) an article-to-money-page matrix assigning each blog post 3-5 internal links toward topically matching service pages, with named source page, target page, and descriptive varied anchor text for each; (4) mini-silos with 2-3 related articles linked at the bottom of each service page, those articles linking back to the service page and to each other; (5) visible link styling, underlined plus a distinct color; (6) menu limited to the most important pages with secondary and legal pages in the footer, and breadcrumbs with BreadcrumbList markup. The plan explains the core rationale: articles capture informational traffic and internal links pass that authority to the pages that convert.

evals.prompt: quick one: https://nordicsupps.fi/collections/creatine-monohydrate is indexed in search console but gets basically zero impressions and zero clicks after 4 months live. it's in the sitemap. i checked and i don't think any page on the site actually links to it, we only push it in our newsletter. why is it dead and how do i fix it?
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis of an orphan page: present in the sitemap but with no inbound internal links, so crawlers revisit it rarely, it accumulates no internal authority, and it is also invisible to AI engines because they retrieve through the search indexes where it has no standing; a sitemap entry is a discovery hint, not a substitute for links. The fix: confirm orphan status with a sitemap-versus-crawl comparison (the skill points to the bundled audit script from the seo-geo-audit skill); add internal links from topically related blog posts and from the parent collection or menu if it is a priority money page, using descriptive varied anchors such as the product category name rather than 'click here' and never one exact-match anchor repeated sitewide; add breadcrumbs with BreadcrumbList markup; style the links visibly (underlined plus distinct color); then re-crawl to verify. The answer should warn against the lazy fix of dumping a sitewide footer link instead of contextual links, and should not drift into buying backlinks, which belongs to the seo-backlinks skill.

evals.prompt: Two questions. Our blog lives at blog.atlasproperty.io while the main site is atlasproperty.io, and we are debating moving it. Also we have two posts, "property management fees explained" (2022, has some backlinks) and "how much do property managers charge" (2024, longer and newer), both stuck on page 2 for basically the same searches. Should we keep both? We sell property management services at https://atlasproperty.io/property-management.
evals.expected_output: Two recommendations. First: migrate the blog from the subdomain to atlasproperty.io/blog with page-level 301 redirects and link it from the menu or footer, stating honestly that Google's public position is that subdomains and subfolders both work and that the subfolder consolidation rule is a field heuristic from agency migration outcomes (authority consolidates on one domain). Second: run the cannibalization test by searching both phrases in Google; if the SERPs overlap substantially the intent is identical, so the two posts must become one page (1 keyword = 1 page). Keep the URL with the most backlinks, age, and impressions (likely the 2022 post given its backlinks and age, which also matters for AI citations since cited pages have a median age around 500 days), merge the newer post's better content into it, and 301 the loser; never delete without a redirect. The merged article should then send 3-5 visible internal links to the property management service page with descriptive anchors, and 2-3 supporting articles should form a mini-silo around that service page, linked from its bottom section and linking back.
